case1_parked_car.description: Parked car hit by third party in mall; missing third-party info and some documents.
case1_parked_car.notes: PDF Case 1. Third-party property damage is covered, but required docs are incomplete.

case2_illegal_racing.description: Confirmed illegal street race crash. Documentation present.
case2_illegal_racing.notes: PDF Case 2. Clear Clause 2.2 exclusion → Rejection review.

case3_theft_no_police.description: Theft from condo parking without a police report.
case3_theft_no_police.notes: PDF Case 3. Theft is covered but police report (Clause 3.2) missing.

case4_fraud_risk.description: Severe damage with weak evidence, 4 claims in 12 months.
case4_fraud_risk.notes: PDF Case 4. Clause 4.3 fraud pattern (repeated claims + weak evidence) must be identified.

case6_th_gear_cable.description: Automatic-transmission gear cable snapped while shifting. Thai customer, from design doc §1.1.
case6_th_gear_cable.notes: Mechanical breakdown without external collision is NOT clearly a covered peril (Clause 1.1 lists accidental collision, theft, fire, flood, third-party damage — not mechanical failure). Strong answers should flag the ambiguity rather than approve.

case7_th_skirt_crack.description: Front skirt chipped from hitting a pothole; single-vehicle, no injury. Thai customer, from design doc §1.1.
case7_th_skirt_crack.notes: Pothole impact can be read as accidental collision (Clause 1.1). Incident report is still required per Clause 3.1. Either Standard processing (if interpreted leniently) or Manual review (if the officer wants to verify the pothole claim) is defensible.

case5_late_submission.description: Flood damage reported 45 days after the incident; no reason given.
case5_late_submission.notes: PDF Case 5. Clause 2.5 exclusion applies (>30 days without valid reason). Strong answers acknowledge uncertainty since manual review may still consider a valid reason.
